summary_en: The Bank of Nagoya raised interim dividend to ¥110 per share (up ¥10) and revised year-end dividend forecast to ¥120 per share (up ¥20), bringing FY2027 total annual dividend to ¥230 per share. The increase reflects stronger-than-expected earnings and maintains the 40% payout ratio target.
title_en: Notice on Dividend Surplus (Interim Dividend) and Revision of Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
On November 13, 2026, The Bank of Nagoya announced an increase in both interim and year-end dividend payouts for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The interim dividend per share was raised by ¥10 to ¥110, with a record date of September 30, 2026 and an effective date of December 11, 2026. The year-end dividend forecast was revised upward by ¥20 per share to ¥120. Consequently, the total annual dividend per share is now projected at ¥230, compared to the previous forecast of ¥200.

The company attributed the increase to stronger-than-expected earnings performance. The parent company's net income attributable to shareholders is now forecast to exceed the earlier projection announced on May 12, 2026. The higher payouts are consistent with the bank's shareholder return policy targeting a payout ratio of approximately 40%.

Note that the company implemented a 3-for-1 stock split effective October 1, 2025 (record date September 30, 2025), and all per-share dividend figures reflect post-split amounts.
